guarantees.claim: hw2reg.val.d is always driven to the value of rx_val_q.
hw2reg.rdata.d is always driven to the value of uart_rdata.
hw2reg.status.rxempty.d is always driven to ~rx_fifo_rvalid (logic 1 when no valid data in RX FIFO).
hw2reg.status.rxidle.d is always driven to rx_uart_idle.
hw2reg.status.txidle.d is always driven to (tx_uart_idle & ~tx_fifo_rvalid), indicating TX is idle only when the UART line is idle and the TX FIFO is empty.
hw2reg.status.txempty.d is always driven to ~tx_fifo_rvalid (logic 1 when TX FIFO has no valid data).
hw2reg.status.rxfull.d is always driven to ~rx_fifo_wready (logic 1 when RX FIFO cannot accept a new write).
hw2reg.status.txfull.d is always driven to ~tx_fifo_wready (logic 1 when TX FIFO cannot accept a new write).
hw2reg.fifo_status.txlvl.d is always driven to 8'(tx_fifo_depth), reporting the current TX FIFO depth level truncated to 8 bits.
hw2reg.fifo_status.rxlvl.d is always driven to 8'(rx_fifo_depth), reporting the current RX FIFO depth level truncated to 8 bits.
hw2reg.fifo_ctrl.rxilvl.de is always driven to 1'b0, disabling any register update from this path.
hw2reg.fifo_ctrl.txilvl.de is always driven to 1'b0, disabling any register update from this path.

assumptions.claim: tx_fifo_depth and rx_fifo_depth are assumed to be ≤ 255 so that the 8' truncation does not lose information.
assumptions.cond: always, when these signals are used to report FIFO levels to software.
assumptions.risk: If depth > 255, the reported txlvl / rxlvl will be an incorrect truncated value, causing software to misjudge FIFO occupancy and potentially leading to overrun or underrun errors.

uncertain_points.claim: hw2reg.fifo_ctrl.rxilvl and .txilvl are continuously driven to 3'h0 with de=0, effectively hardwiring the FIFO trigger levels to zero and preventing any software writes. The comment mentions ‘resets are self-clearing’, but it is unclear whether these fields should be programmable after reset.
uncertain_points.risk: If these fields are intended to be programmable FIFO level thresholds (as typical in UARTs), the constant zero values will completely disable level‑triggered interrupts and may cause firmware to stall or miss transfer completions. This is a direct functional break of the FIFO control feature.

uncertain_points.claim: tx_fifo_depth and rx_fifo_depth are cast to 8 bits with 8'(). If the actual FIFO depth can exceed 255 (e.g., through parameterization), the reported level is truncated.
uncertain_points.cond: when the parameterized FIFO depth is greater than 255.
uncertain_points.risk: Truncated level values misrepresent FIFO occupancy to software, potentially causing decisions based on incorrect fullness/empty status, which can lead to data loss or deadlock.
